recommended_tasks:
To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- A manual D-1 estimate is prepared for under 30% of dry SKUs, without a system-run ARS
- Same-day adjustment, where it happens, is ad hoc and not demand-triggered

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- A D-1 automated run covers 30-60% of dry SKU replenishment volume
- A defined (if not yet optimal) same-day top-up step exists for the remainder
- Planning-to-dispatch window is documented and tracked weekly

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- D-1 ARS run covers 60-90% of dry SKU replenishment volume
- The same-day second pass is demand-triggered (not clock-triggered) for over 60% of that pass
- Resulting stockout rate held under 5% and overstock rate under 8%, tracked weekly

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- D-1 ARS run covers over 90% of dry SKU volume, targeting ~70% of the day's total dry quantity
- The remaining ~30% is committed via a same-day, fully demand-triggered second pass
- Stockout rate under 2% and overstock rate under 4%, both tracked in real time
- Zero manual overrides to the ARS output without a logged reason

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- A same-day adjustment for FnV happens, but only reactively once a stockout or dump is already visible

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- At least 1 same-day FnV replanning cycle runs daily, using prior-day sales as the basis (not yet live same-day signals)

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- 2 or more same-day FnV replanning cycles run daily
- Live same-day sales/wastage data is incorporated for over 60% of FnV SKUs

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- FnV replenishment runs on 2+ same-day cycles fully driven by live demand and shelf-life data for over 90% of FnV SKUs
- FnV dump/shrinkage rate attributable to over-replenishment held under 3%

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Reorder-point triggers defined for under 20% of SKUs; safety stock not lead-time-adjusted

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Reorder-point triggers cover 20-50% of SKUs
- Safety stock is lead-time-adjusted for the dry category only

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Reorder-point triggers cover 50-90% of SKUs across both dry and FnV
- Safety stock is lead-time-adjusted for both categories

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Reorder-point triggers cover over 90% of SKUs
- Safety stock is dynamically lead-time- and variability-adjusted per SKU, reviewed at least monthly

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Forecast informs replenishment for under 20% of SKUs, applied inconsistently

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- A forecast-derived formula (Forecast Demand + Safety Stock - Current Inventory) covers 20-60% of SKUs
- Reviewed periodically for linkage accuracy

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Formula-driven linkage covers 60-90% of SKUs
- Manual override rate held under 15%, reviewed weekly

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Formula-driven linkage covers over 90% of SKUs with automated recalculation as the forecast updates
- Manual override rate under 5%, logged with reason, tracked in real time

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Emergency top-ups happen but are entirely ad hoc, with no defined trigger or owner

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- A manually-invoked emergency top-up procedure is defined and used
- Invoked for more than 10% of replenishment cycles

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Emergency top-up is bound to a defined SLA (e.g. dispatched within 4 hours of trigger)
- Invoked for under 10% of cycles, tracked weekly

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Emergency top-up is fully integrated into the automated replenishment system with SLA-bound, system-triggered activation
- Invoked for under 3% of cycles

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Frequency varies informally by category (e.g. "FnV gets more"), without a documented velocity/shelf-life-based rule

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- A documented frequency band exists (e.g. high-velocity dry: 1 cycle/day, FnV: 2 cycles/day)
- Applied to over 50% of SKUs

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Frequency bands cover over 80% of SKUs
- Reviewed quarterly against actual velocity/shelf-life data

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Frequency is dynamically tuned per SKU by real-time velocity, shelf-life, and dark-store inventory position for over 90% of SKUs

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- DoI is tracked by category (dry vs FnV) but not by individual SKU, and no target band is defined

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- DoI is tracked by SKU weekly against a defined target band, for the dry category only

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- DoI is tracked by SKU daily against a target band for both dry and FnV, with breaches flagged

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- DoI is tracked by SKU in real time against a target band for both categories
- Breaches are auto-flagged and root-caused within the day

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- The window is known informally for a few high-profile SKUs/routes but not tracked as a standing metric

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Planning-to-dispatch lead time is tracked weekly at an aggregate level

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Lead time is tracked per replenishment cycle (D-1 and same-day passes separately)
- Delays over a defined threshold (e.g. 2 hours) are flagged

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Lead time is tracked in real time per cycle with automated alerts on threshold breach
- Monthly root-cause review of chronic delay sources

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- An informal sense of when more capacity is needed exists but isn't written down or tied to volume.
- changes happen reactively after a problem shows up.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Current hub/lane structure has a documented volume-based rationale, and a defined volume threshold exists for adding a new hub/lane.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Hub/lane design is reviewed against current demand data on a regular cadence (e.g. quarterly), with thresholds tied to average and peak/seasonal volume.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Network design is proactively modeled against forecasted demand growth and geography shifts, with changes planned ahead of the threshold being hit.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Basic manual grouping of nearby stops happens sometimes, but inconsistently and without a defined method.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A defined method (manual or tool-assisted) is used to sequence multi-stop routes based on geography and volume.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Route optimization is software-assisted and reviewed regularly against actual vs. planned stop efficiency.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Routes are dynamically re-optimized using live data (traffic, order changes, vehicle availability), continuously improving stop efficiency.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Assignment logic exists informally (e.g. "nearest hub") but isn't calculated or reviewed

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Assignment is calculated against distance/cost for over 50% of dark stores
- Reviewed only at network-change events

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Assignment covers over 90% of dark stores, reviewed quarterly as the network grows

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Assignment is continuously re-optimized as new dark stores/hubs are added
- 100% of dark stores are served by their cost/distance-optimal node

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- A rough wave schedule exists but isn't tied to volume/demand data
- Vehicle size is chosen by habit; under 20% of waves have a vehicle size matching actual load within +/-20%

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Wave structure is documented and designed against average daily volume distribution
- Vehicle-size-to-volume match rate is 40-60%, tracked monthly

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Wave structure is reviewed and adjusted regularly against actual volume patterns, including peak periods
- Vehicle-size-to-volume match rate is 60-85%, with mismatches root-caused monthly

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Wave architecture is dynamically adjusted based on real-time order flow and downstream consumption patterns
- Vehicle-size-to-volume match rate exceeds 90%, benchmarked against industry practice (e.g. a fleet mix tiered by dark-store volume band)

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Readiness is attempted informally but wait times are inconsistent and untracked.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Vehicle wait time for cargo readiness is measured and tracked against a target.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Staging/picking is scheduled to align with vehicle arrival times, with wait time root-caused when it exceeds target.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Wave readiness is tightly synchronized with vehicle ETAs (dock scheduling, pre-staging), minimizing wait time to near zero.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Some awareness exists that timing matters, but waves aren't deliberately aligned to demand windows.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Wave departure times are mapped against known downstream demand windows for most waves.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Wave-to-demand alignment is tracked and adjusted regularly as downstream demand patterns shift.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Wave timing is dynamically optimized against real-time downstream demand signals across the network.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Capacity is planned informally against volume but not reviewed regularly.
- gaps happen often and are covered reactively, however they're covered.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Total capacity (owned, contracted, and spot combined) is documented against average daily dispatch volume and reviewed monthly, with a clear, deliberate rationale for how much of it is committed vs. spot.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Capacity planning covers average and peak volume, with the committed/spot split explicitly matched to how predictable volume is right now (e.g. a fast-growing lane deliberately leaning on spot.
- a stable lane deliberately leaning on committed capacity).

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Capacity planning is dynamically adjusted to forecasted volume including seasonal/event peaks, with the committed/spot mix continuously re-optimized as each lane's predictability and the business's capital position evolve.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
A mix exists, but it's a byproduct of circumstance (whatever was available when scaling started) rather than a deliberate choice, and isn't tracked against actuals.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A target mix is documented and explicitly justified against the business's current stage - e.g. a growing business deliberately leaning contracted/spot for flexibility and capital efficiency, or a mature business with stable volume deliberately leaning owned/contracted for lower steady-state cost. Tracked monthly against actuals.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
The mix is actively revisited on a regular cadence as volume predictability and capital position evolve, with a pre-agreed trigger for when the target mix itself should shift (e.g. once a lane's volume is stable for two quarters, move it from spot to contract).

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
The mix is continuously optimized using live cost, demand-predictability, and capital-cost signals, with the owned/contracted/spot balance an explicit, revisited decision at every stage - not a default set once and never questioned.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
A backup vendor is contacted only once a shortage is already identified.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A defined backup arrangement exists and is engaged proactively before a shortfall causes a missed dispatch, sized to the business's actual peak-risk exposure rather than a fixed headcount.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Backup coverage is tested periodically with response-time expectations agreed in advance, proportionate to how much volume/revenue is genuinely at risk from a shortage.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Backup readiness is continuously maintained and tested, scaled dynamically as volume and peak-risk grow - without over-investing in standby capacity beyond what current exposure justifies.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate known anecdotally (not tracked as a number); estimated 50-65% based on informal observation

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate measured and tracked monthly against a 70% target

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate tracked per lane/vehicle type, held at 70-85%
- Chronic sub-70% trips root-caused

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate optimized dynamically (load consolidation, wave timing)
- Consistently at or above 90% of rated capacity

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Empty-running is acknowledged as a problem and backhaul is used occasionally, but only when a driver/dispatcher happens to notice an opportunity - nothing is measured or planned.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Empty-running % is tracked with a reduction target, and backhaul planning is a defined step in trip planning with its own tracked utilization rate.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Empty-running is actively reduced through systematic backhaul planning and route redesign, reviewed monthly against target across most lanes.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Empty-running is minimized network-wide through continuous backhaul/route optimization, tracked in real time and sitting near the practical ceiling for the network's shape.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Turnaround time is known informally for a few routes but not tracked systematically.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Turnaround time is measured per trip and tracked against a target.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Turnaround time is tracked per lane/vehicle, with bottleneck stages (loading, dock wait, unloading) identified and addressed.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Turnaround time is continuously monitored and optimized, with trips-per-vehicle-per-day maximized against a defined ceiling.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
On-time arrival is tracked loosely/manually, without a consistent definition of 'on time'.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
On-time arrival % is tracked systematically against a defined SLA window, reviewed monthly.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
On-time arrival is tracked per lane with root-cause analysis for chronic misses.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
On-time arrival is tracked in real time with predictive ETA alerts, enabling proactive downstream replanning before a miss occurs.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Cancellations are known anecdotally but not logged or reviewed.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Trip completion rate is tracked and reviewed monthly against a target.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Cancelled/failed trips are root-caused and tracked to closure.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Trip completion rate is tracked in real time with automated failure alerts and near-zero unexplained cancellations.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Average transit time is tracked per lane, but variability/consistency is not measured.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Both average and variability (e.g. std. deviation) of transit time are tracked per lane against an SLA.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
High-variability lanes are identified and root-caused, with corrective action tracked to closure.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Transit time variability is continuously monitored and actively engineered down through route/schedule design.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Unit costs calculated occasionally/manually but not tracked as a standing metric
- No visibility into the gap vs the ~Rs 0.78/unit blended benchmark (FnV segment ~Rs 0.91/unit, Dry ~Rs 0.70/unit)

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Cost per km, per trip, and per unit moved is tracked monthly against an internal baseline
- Current blended cost is approximately Rs 1.00/unit, tracked but not yet actively closed against the Rs 0.78/unit benchmark

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Unit costs tracked per lane/vehicle type, with variance from both the internal baseline and the Rs 0.78/unit benchmark investigated monthly
- A documented gap-closure plan exists

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Unit costs tracked in near-real-time with automated variance alerts
- Blended cost per unit at or below the Rs 0.78/unit benchmark, or a documented, funded, time-bound plan is in place to reach it

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Some lanes are known informally to be expensive, but it isn't quantified or reviewed.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Cost-to-serve per lane is calculated and compared against network average on a defined cadence.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Structurally expensive lanes are flagged and have a documented improvement or pricing action plan.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Lane-level cost-to-serve is continuously monitored and factored into network design and pricing decisions.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Spot-hire cost is known to be higher but isn't quantified as a % of spend or understood as a deliberate trade-off.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Spot-hire premium is tracked monthly as a % of total spend, with a clear view of why that level is being paid - flexibility trade-off vs. avoidable inefficiency.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Spot-hire premium is broken down by lane/period to separate deliberate flexibility spend (e.g. a new, unproven lane) from avoidable spend (a stable lane that should have moved to contract), with a plan to shift the avoidable portion.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Spot-hire premium is actively managed as a strategic lever - deliberately kept higher on immature/volatile lanes for flexibility, and driven down on stable lanes - tracked in near real time.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Temperature is checked at dispatch only, not monitored continuously through the trip.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Temperature is logged continuously during transit, with breach incidents recorded and reviewed monthly.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Breach incidents are root-caused and tracked to closure, with recurring causes addressed (e.g. vehicle maintenance, driver training).

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Temperature is monitored in real time with automated breach alerts, enabling in-trip corrective action before product is compromised.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
In-transit loss is estimated informally but not measured as a distinct, tracked %.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
In-transit damage/spoilage % is tracked monthly as its own metric, separate from warehouse/last-mile loss.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Root causes of in-transit loss (handling, temperature, route condition) are investigated and addressed.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
In-transit loss is tracked in near-real-time with proactive interventions (packaging, handling protocol, route choice) driving it toward zero.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Dock dwell time is known anecdotally to be an issue but not measured.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Dock dwell time is measured per trip and tracked against a target.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Dwell time is tracked per dock/lane, with chronic delays root-caused and addressed.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Dwell time is actively minimized through dock scheduling/slotting and monitored in real time.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Some vehicles have GPS tracking, but coverage is partial and inconsistently used.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
The fleet serving critical/high-volume lanes has live GPS/ETA visibility through a defined, cost-appropriate system.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Tracking coverage extends across the full active fleet, integrated into a control tower view used for daily ops decisions.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Real-time tracking with predictive ETA is standard fleet-wide and drives automated downstream alerts/replanning.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Exceptions are sometimes caught by a dispatcher noticing manually, with no defined detection process.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A defined process/system flags exceptions (delay, deviation, breakdown) against expected trip progress.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Exception detection is systematic and tracked, with average time-to-detect measured and improved.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Exceptions are detected automatically in near-real-time via system alerts, minimizing detection lag to minutes.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
An informal escalation habit exists but isn't documented or consistently followed.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A defined escalation path and SLA exist for exceptions, with adherence tracked.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Escalation SLA adherence is tracked and chronic misses are root-caused.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Escalation is largely automated (auto-routing to the right owner) with near-100% SLA adherence, tracked in real time.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Performance is discussed informally with carriers but not scored or documented.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- A defined scorecard (on-time %, cost, compliance) covers over 70% of carrier spend, reviewed quarterly

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Scorecard results directly inform volume allocation and contract renewal decisions.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Scorecarding is continuous and data-driven, with allocation dynamically shifted toward top performers.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Some single-vendor dependencies are known informally, but there's no view of which ones are genuinely high-risk given current volume.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Lanes/regions carrying real risk (highest volume, or hardest to re-source quickly) are identified, with a documented backup plan - even where a second vendor isn't yet economically justified for lower-risk lanes.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Backup coverage is proportionate to risk and actively verified (not just listed) for the highest-risk lanes, with a clear trigger for when a growing lane earns a formal second vendor.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Vendor risk is continuously monitored across the network, with backup depth scaled to each lane's volume/criticality rather than applied uniformly everywhere.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Accidents are logged after the fact, but near-misses/unsafe behavior aren't captured.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Incidents (accidents and near-misses) are tracked and reviewed against a benchmark rate.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Root causes of incidents are analyzed and used to drive targeted driver training/interventions.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Safety performance is monitored proactively (e.g. telematics-based driver scoring), with incident rates trending toward best-in-class.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Documentation exists but expiry isn't proactively monitored.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A tracked register covers all active vehicles' compliance documents with expiry dates.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Automated reminders/alerts prevent lapses before they occur, tracked against a near-100% compliance target.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Compliance is continuously monitored and audited, with zero tolerance for lapses enforced systematically.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Driving hours are logged manually but not systematically checked against limits.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Driving hours are tracked and checked against regulatory limits for all trips.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Violations are root-caused (e.g. scheduling, route length) and addressed via planning changes.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Driving hours are monitored in real time (e.g. via telematics) with automated alerts preventing violations before they occur.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Shelf availability is checked manually at least once a shift, without a system-tracked %

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Shelf availability is tracked via the inventory system for over 50% of SKUs, reviewed twice daily
- Stockout duration tracked weekly

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Shelf availability tracked in real time for over 90% of SKUs with automated low-stock alerts
- Stockout duration root-caused daily

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Shelf availability tracked in real time for 100% of SKUs, held above 98%
- Stockouts root-caused same-day, feeding continuous reorder-point recalibration (RM1.3)

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate is tracked only on escalation, not as a standing weekly metric

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate tracked weekly at the dark-store level, for the dry category only

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate tracked daily at the dark-store level for both dry and FnV, held above 90%

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Fill rate tracked in real time per dark store per SKU, consistently exceeding 97%

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
- Stock-out and excess incidents are noted informally when they occur, without a standing % metric

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
- Both rates tracked weekly at the dark-store level for over 50% of SKUs, against the DoI target band from RM2.2

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
- Both rates tracked daily per dark store per SKU
- Root-caused for over 90% of incidents (forecast error, replenishment frequency, or shelf-life)
- Resulting wastage is quantified

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
- Both rates tracked in real time per SKU, held within a tight target band, root-caused same-day
- The stock-out-vs-excess trade-off is actively and continuously optimized across the dark-store network

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Root-causing happens occasionally, informally, for the most visible failures only.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
A defined root-cause process covers major incident types, with findings documented.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Root-causing is systematic and covers most incidents, feeding into a tracked improvement backlog.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Root-causing is standard practice for all significant incidents, with findings driving proactive process redesign.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Some corrective actions are tracked, but closure isn't consistently followed up.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Corrective actions are tracked to closure with a defined target closure time.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Closure time is measured and reviewed monthly, with overdue actions escalated.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Corrective action closure is fast and reliably tracked, with closure time trending toward best-in-class benchmarks.

To reach Level 2 (Basic), ensure the following are true:
Recurrence is noticed anecdotally but not measured.

To reach Level 3 (Standardized), ensure the following are true:
Recurrence rate (same root cause reappearing within a defined window) is tracked.

To reach Level 4 (Managed), ensure the following are true:
Recurring issues are flagged for deeper structural fixes rather than repeated point fixes.

To reach Level 5 (Best-in-class), ensure the following are true:
Recurrence is actively monitored and trending toward zero, validating that fixes address true root causes.
